accessibility_source_findings.finding: No skip-to-content link anywhere; keyboard users tab through the 20-link desktop sidebar and the StatsBar before reaching <main> on every route.

Single-character shortcuts A/R/S write a review decision immediately with no confirmation, no undo and no way to disable or remap (WCAG 2.1.4). The handler only ignores input/textarea/combobox targets, so the keys fire while focus is on any button or link on the page.

The review 'cursor' row that A/R/S act on is a non-focusable <div> styled by border only; it has no tabindex, aria-current/aria-selected or live announcement, so assistive-technology users cannot tell which record a shortcut will decide. It is also independent of DOM focus.

Toasts are plain <div>s with no role=status/alert or aria-live, yet they are the only success/failure feedback for review decisions, regulatory decisions, export, notify, hydromet refresh and API-key changes. The toast close button is icon-only with no accessible name and is opacity-0 until hover/focus.
Review Queue severity and tier Select triggers (role=combobox) have no aria-label. Same defect on the Live Logs type filter and the Outages type filter.

AI panel close button and send button are icon-only with no accessible name; the text input has only a placeholder; the panel is not a dialog/region, has no label and no focus management on open/close.

Mobile navigation is a full-screen fixed <aside> without role=dialog/aria-modal, focus is not moved into it or returned on close, and background content stays in the tab order. Group tabs use role=tab/tablist without tabpanel, aria-controls or arrow-key handling.

Map page uses a fixed 440px non-shrinking aside beside a flex-1 min-w-0 map with no responsive breakpoint, and a 250px layer panel over the map; at phone widths the map column collapses. Monitoring has the same pattern with a fixed 250px layer rail.
The main map container has no role or accessible name, and marker/polygon selection, hover popups and all spatial tools are pointer-only (map.on('click'/'mouseenter')).
78 focusable SVG municipio paths remove the focus outline (focus:outline-none) and provide no alternative focus style; they also add 78 tab stops with no roving tabindex.
Basemap Map/Satellite buttons expose the active choice by colour only (no aria-pressed), unlike the other layer toggles. Monitoring range buttons and water-layer rail buttons have the same gap.
Overview and Map routes render no <h1> (neither uses PageHeader); the desktop sidebar's <h2> group headings precede any page heading in DOM order.
WaterDisruption renders its own <main> inside the layout's <main>, producing nested main landmarks.
Mobile header and StatsBar are <div>s; there is no <header>/banner landmark. Backend-down banner has no role=alert/aria-live.

In the mobile drawer the top-level NavLink ignores isActive for styling (always 'text-xl text-sky-700'); the current page is conveyed only by react-router's implicit aria-current, with no visible indication for top-level items.
Several icon-only buttons rely on `title` alone for a name: Review CSV export, Review AI-suggest, Assets CSV export.
Review row selection and 'Select all on page' are plain buttons swapping icons; no role=checkbox/aria-checked/aria-pressed, and every row's button has the same name 'Select record'.

Regulatory 'Approve' is disabled when contradictions exist and the reason is given only through a title attribute on a disabled button (not focusable, not announced); the form itself gives no inline reason for disabled Reject/Needs-review when actor/rationale are empty.

special_adjudications.answer: Controls per row: select toggle (button, aria-label 'Select record'/'Deselect record'), AI-suggest (icon-only, title 'Ask AI for a recommendation', no aria-label), Accept (visible text), Reject (visible text), Skip (icon-only, aria-label 'Skip'). Header when rows are selected: 'Approve all', 'Reject all', 'Skip all'; plus 'Select all on page'/'Deselect all'. All are native <button>s, so Tab/Enter/Space work. Global window shortcuts: J/K or arrows move a visual cursor, A/R/S decide the cursor row; ignored only inside input/textarea/combobox/contenteditable. Confirmation: none for single, keyboard or batch decisions; no undo. Optimistic removal with rollback on error (lib/hooks.js:89-101). Failure reporting: a thrown error (401 or network/timeout) shows a destructive toast titled only 'Decision failed' — the error message, which distinguishes 'key missing' from 'key rejected', is discarded. Any other HTTP status is NOT detected: postDecision returns res.json() without checking res.ok, so a 400/404/500 with a JSON body yields the success toast 'Marked <decision>'. Batch reports 'N items processed' regardless of individual failures. Toasts have no live region. Persistence: the backend keeps decisions only in the module-level dict `_decisions` ('survives only until server restart'); nothing is written to outputs/review_queue.json or any ledger, no actor is recorded, and 'skip' is stored but not excluded from GET /review-queue, so a skipped row reappears after the refetch. Authorization: Bearer API_SECRET_KEY when that env var is set, otherwise open.
special_adjudications.question: 3a. Review Queue (/review): decision controls, names, keyboard, confirmation, failed-write reporting, persistence

special_adjudications.answer: Controls: decision-state filter Select (aria-label 'Filter by decision state'); candidate list of <button aria-pressed>; form with labelled 'Actor' text input and 'Rationale' textarea; three buttons with visible text — 'Approve', 'Reject' (destructive variant), 'Mark needs review'. All native controls, keyboard operable; no shortcuts. Guards instead of a confirmation dialog: all three are disabled until actor and rationale are non-empty and while submitting; Approve is additionally disabled when the candidate has contradictions (reason exposed only as a title attribute). No confirm step and no undo, but a later decision can overwrite. Failure reporting: postRegulatoryLinkDecision throws on 401 (key missing vs rejected), 422 (lists contradiction details) and any other non-2xx ('Decision failed (status)'), and the page shows a destructive toast 'Decision failed' with err.message; rationale is kept on failure and cleared on success. Network errors also reach the catch. Toast has no live region. Read failures are masked: list fetch failures return an empty list so the page says 'No candidates match the current filter'. Persistence: NOT memory-only — the handler writes the decided row (decision_state, decided_at, decided_by, decision_rationale) through write_regulatory_links, which schema-validates and rewrites the links JSONL. Authorization: Bearer API_SECRET_KEY when set.

special_adjudications.answer: /map: no handling for basemap, glyph or terrain tile failure — the only map 'error' listener filters to NWS overlay sources and ignores everything else; there is no offline/blank-basemap message and no try/catch around map construction. Data layers are attached on 'style.load' rather than 'load' so they still draw when raster tiles never arrive (stated in a code comment). NWS overlays do report per-overlay loading/live/error text in an aria-live region, and tile URLs carry a 5-minute cache-busting bucket. Data-fetch failure: event density shows the error with a 'Retry density' button; rainfall error text is passed in as a prop; assets/municipios/alerts/gauges GeoJSON failures silently become empty FeatureCollections (getJSON fallback) and the map just shows fewer features. /monitoring HydroMapWorkspace: construction is wrapped in try/catch ('Map unavailable: …'), every map error (including tile errors) is collected into a role=alert list (max 6), and the offline export shows an explicit placeholder. Overview SVG map: no tiles; shows 'Municipal geometry is unavailable.' when geometry is missing and a contract warning when not exactly 78 features.

special_adjudications.answer: Pipeline.jsx uses cards, not a table. Container 'max-w-7xl mx-auto px-4 py-8 space-y-8' (:101); stats row 'flex flex-wrap gap-4' (:110); domain chips 'flex flex-wrap gap-2' (:129) so the 8 chips wrap rather than scroll; list 'grid gap-3 md:grid-cols-2' (:157), i.e. one column below Tailwind md (768px) and two above; badges 'flex flex-wrap' (:58). There is no overflow-x handling on the page. The shell collapses at 820px (AppShell.module.css:185-188) and sets min-width:0 on workspace/main (AppShell.module.css:113-115; adaptation.css:4-5). Overflow risk is present by source reading: below md the grid has a single implicit auto track and each card link is a grid item with 'block' but no min-w-0 (:49); the title inside is 'truncate' i.e. nowrap (:53) and the min-w-0 sits on an inner flex child (:52), which does not reduce the grid item's content-based minimum. A long title can therefore widen the track beyond the viewport; at md and above grid-cols-2 uses minmax(0,1fr) and the problem disappears. This matches the mobile-only overflow recorded in docs/A11Y_AUDIT.md:59-61, though that document attributes it to the chip bar, which does wrap. Not run, so this is an inference from CSS rules. PipelineItemDetail also has a 'grid grid-cols-2' metadata block with an unbroken monospace item_id (PipelineItemDetail.jsx:146-147) that can spill at narrow widths.

accessibility_source_findings.finding: At <=760px (which the 420px-wide desktop window reaches) the closed navigation panel is only translated off-screen; it is not display:none, visibility:hidden or inert. Its ~10+ buttons stay in the tab order and the accessibility tree, so keyboard focus disappears off-screen before reaching the page content. When open it is not a dialog: no focus move into it, no focus trap, no Escape, no close button, and the toggle keeps the label 'Open navigation'.

Functional, affects all users: runs with more than 500 events are reloaded with only the first 500 (see workflow stream-answer), which removes the tail of a long live-streamed answer and its citations.

The conversation menu declares role=menu/menuitem but implements none of the pattern: focus is not moved into it, there is no arrow-key navigation, Escape or outside-click close; it stays open until an item or the toggle is pressed.

The mode picker is a ul role=listbox whose children are plain li elements wrapping button role=option (invalid ownership), with no arrow keys, Escape or active-descendant; it works as a list of buttons by Tab only.

Sheet returns focus to the element focused when it mounted. For sheets opened from the conversation menu (Rename, Delete, Background tasks) that element is a menu item that has already been unmounted, so focus falls to the document body on close. Same for the approval card: after Allow/Deny the card unmounts and nothing receives focus.

The trap's focusable selector omits <summary> and matches elements inside closed <details> (e.g. pre[tabindex=0]). In sheets that end with disclosures (Tool activity, Evidence) the computed last item can be an unfocusable hidden element, so Tab from the last visible control can leave the dialog; the page behind is not inert or aria-hidden (aria-modal only).
Switching workspace does not move focus, change document.title or announce; a screen-reader user gets only aria-current on the pressed button. The page title is always 'Mucaro AI'.

special_adjudications.answer: Functional but read-only and narrow; not presentational. It has no props, no buttons, inputs, links or handlers of its own: the only controls are one native <details>/<summary> 'Record' per tool call. On mount it makes two calls. GET /tools/summary returns counts by status computed from the stored tool-call records plus a live verification of the hash-chained audit log; the UI shows 'Verified (N events)' or the broken status and reason in error styling. GET /tools/requests returns every stored tool call; the UI lists them newest first with status, tool name, created time and, behind the disclosure, requested_by, approved_by, denied_by, argument digest, run id and raw arguments/result JSON. Both are real persisted data. special_adjudications.answer: Rendering: the client reads server-sent events with fetch, de-duplicates by seq and concatenates text_delta events into the answer, rendered as inert text with fenced code blocks; the run article is aria-busy while RUNNING and the feed auto-scrolls only when already near the bottom. The streaming text is not a live region; 'Answer complete.' is announced at the end. Save and Share appear only on terminal runs; Copy and Edit are offered while still streaming. Cancel: Stop calls POST /work-runs/{id}/stop. Waiting runs stop at once; a running run is flagged and stops at the next phase boundary, but the answer phase has no checkpoint, so Stop does not interrupt text that is already streaming and the run still ends COMPLETED. Model/provider error mid-answer: the backend records error and final(FAILED) events; text_delta events already written stay in the log, so the partial text remains above an alert showing category, status and detail, and 'The turn failed.' is announced. Disconnect: a stream that fails, closes without an end event or is silent for 25 s is retried with backoff (reloading the run from the event log each time); after 10 failures a 'Live updates paused' notice with Resume appears; the app-level banner shows 'Reconnecting…' from the 15 s health poll, and returning to the page or regaining network forces a re-follow. Partial output is preserved because events are persisted server-side. A service restart marks running runs INTERRUPTED. Defect by source reading: runs with more than 500 events are reloaded truncated to the first 500 (see workflow stream-answer).
special_adjudications.question: 6. Streaming: rendering, cancel, mid-stream error or disconnect, partial output

special_adjudications.answer: Tool-request approval is complete. The card is a labelled region ('Permission request for <tool>') showing the tool, who asked, arguments (patches as a diff) and the argument digest, with native Deny and Allow once buttons. They POST /tools/requests/{id}/approve or /deny with arguments_sha256. The backend refuses a non-pending call or a digest mismatch, stores status with approved_by/denied_by and a timestamp on the tool-call record, appends a hash-chained audit event, and resumes the run. Both buttons work from the keyboard; the waiting state is announced ('Waiting for your approval.') and the decision is announced ('Allowed/Denied <tool>.') through the polite live region, and the conversation list shows 'Needs your approval'. Focus is not moved to the card and is lost when it disappears. The actor recorded is the constant 'api'. The Planning-to-Execution Gate named in README and docs/EXECUTION_GATE.md (POST /plan, POST /approve) has no GUI: the Workbench only compiles a plan with approval NOT_REQUESTED and states that nothing is executed. The GUI gate that does exist is the execution-entry card: Proceed/Execute and Adjust/Revise post a decision bound to artifact, revision, expected version, source commit and an idempotency key; the decision and receipt hashes are persisted and shown in the Execution receipt sheet. The primary button is natively disabled with an aria-describedby reason until the entry is ready and the source identity is current, it activates from the keyboard, and 'Execution started.' is announced. But the GUI can neither create an entry nor mark one ready, so this gate is usable only for entries prepared through the API.

accessibility_source_findings.finding: On desktop the only ways to open a case are a mouse click on a <tr> that has no tabIndex, role or key handler, or a click on a map canvas point. The case detail cannot be opened from the keyboard or by a screen-reader user in the desktop shell.

A failed or still-pending /cases or /geojson request is presented as real emptiness ('0 of 0 cases', 'No cases found', '0 mapped sightings'). Only the small header text says 'backend unreachable'. Statistics and Candidates do distinguish the two states through QueryState.

The MapLibre container has no role or accessible name, and points, clusters and all three spatial tools respond only to pointer clicks. The Cases list is a text equivalent for the points themselves, but not for measure, buffer or nearest.

Both Recharts bar charts expose their per-decade and per-tier values only as SVG bars and hover tooltips; there is no table, list or accessibilityLayer. Only Total/Mapped/Unmapped are available as text.

special_adjudications.answer: Storage: window.localStorage key 'federation_write_token' (federationClient.js:13,18-27), plus an in-memory copy appParams.writeToken captured at module load (app-params.js:84). The only way it gets set is the URL query parameter ?write_token=..., which getParamValue writes to localStorage under federation_write_token and then strips from the URL via history.replaceState (app-params.js:35-49,84); ?clear_write_token=true removes it (app-params.js:64-66). It is sent as 'Authorization: Bearer' only when no access token is present (federationClient.js:65-66,72-74). UI entry: NONE - there is no input, form or settings surface for the token; setWriteToken is exported but has no caller (grep setWriteToken in src: definition only). The backend exposes public_settings.write_token_required (main.py:1108) but the frontend never reads it, so the UI cannot prompt; the only user-facing hint is the Review-queue 401/403 message 'Reviewing needs write access (a local network, or the PRII write token).' (SkyCameras.jsx:305). Token persists in localStorage in plaintext with no expiry. The backend comment at main.py:309-312 ('browser UI has no write-credential input ... sources only the federation access token') is partly stale: the client now does source a separate write token, but still offers no input.

special_adjudications.answer: The mechanism named in the old audit (whenStyleReady gated on map.isStyleLoaded) no longer exists; the runtime now resolves `ready` on the style.load event and layer hooks add sources directly. Loading is set at SI:255 (GeoJSON layers) and SI:326 (Martin vector layer); it is cleared by 'source-ready' (263/342), 'loaded' (267/352), 'error' (270/355, and 320 for tile errors) and 'idle' when toggled off (246/313). Paths on which it is NOT cleared: (1) hung request — both hooks use bare fetch with an AbortSignal but no timeout (257, 328), so a backend that accepts the connection and never answers leaves 'loading…' indefinitely; (2) abort/cancel — the catch and the post-await guards return without writing a status (260, 264, 269 / 341, 343, 354); when the cleanup is caused by a 2D→3D switch or a runtime reboot the effect re-runs with mapRef.current === null and returns at 236/303 before any onStatus call, so the last status ('loading…', 'source ready' or 'rendered') stays on the button for as long as 3D is active, and the layer buttons are still rendered in 3D (867-883) while the failure banner is 2D-only (848); (3) 'source-ready' is terminal if map.getSource(sourceId) is already true at 264/343; (4) two hooks write the same 'municipios' key: with Martin delivery the vector hook sets 'loading' and the disabled GeoJSON hook then sets 'idle' in the same commit (313 vs 246, declared at 477-496), so the button reads 'on' rather than 'loading…' until the fetch settles; (5) empty result — an empty FeatureCollection (backend returns one for any allowed layer with no file, main.py:472) is reported as 'rendered' with no empty indication; (6) vector layer 'loaded' is set when the source is added, not when tiles arrive, so missing tiles show 'rendered' unless MapLibre raises an error event carrying sourceId. Unmount is safe (state is discarded; cleanup aborts and removes layers, 275-279). Related flags with the same no-timeout weakness: gazetteer density (614-617) and the ERI catalog (spatial/imagery/eriApi.ts:65) which also suppresses URL-hash writes while loading (useImageryController.ts:135). Access-point registries use fetchWithTimeout but 'Records received; drawing…' never advances when the map is not ready (e.g. WebGL unavailable: activeMode stays 'maplibre' with ready=false, useSpatialRuntime.ts:60-70, so the panel is shown and the draw effect returns at useAccessPointsController.ts:121).

special_adjudications.answer: The silent-blank case is fixed in the client and covered by four tests: HTTP error → 'RAG backend returned <status>'; no body → 'returned no response stream'; done event with non-zero rc → 'RAG backend exited with code N'; rc 0 with no data lines → 'completed without producing output'; stream closed without a done event → 'ended without terminal status'; malformed done payload → 'invalid terminal status'; transport error/8 s header timeout → the exception text. Each calls onError then onDone, and QueryLayer renders a role=alert 'Query failed' card with the message plus a hint to switch to STUB; partial output stays visible below it. query_llm.py now exists at the repo root as a wrapper. What is still not useful: (a) the backend opens the subprocess with stderr=PIPE and never reads it, so the reason for a non-zero exit (traceback, missing model/dependency) never reaches the user — only the exit code does; an unread stderr pipe can also fill and block the child, in which case no done event is ever sent; (b) while pending and before the first token the panel shows nothing at all — no response card (needs streamLines.length > 0), no 'No query run yet' card (needs !pending) — only the button reading STOP; there is no overall timeout on the stream; (c) STOP/unmount only sets a cancelled flag: the fetch is not aborted and the generator has no cleanup to terminate the subprocess; (d) query_llm prints progress lines ('Loading model…', 'Retrieving relevant posts…', '====') to stdout, which are streamed to the user as answer text, and any one such line satisfies the 'produced output' check; (e) the error card persists after switching back to STUB until the next run.

special_adjudications.answer: Exhaustive list of deferral points in non-test source: (1) six React.lazy module chunks in App.tsx — CommandCenter, FinanceIntelligence (defers @tanstack/react-table), SpatialIntelligence (defers maplibre-gl JS, the @turf/* packages, Zod-based imagery/access-point clients via its static imports), AnomalyWorkbench, InvestigationGraph, QueryLayer — rendered inside one Suspense with a 'Loading module…' fallback and a per-module ErrorBoundary; (2) one dynamic import, RuntimeFactory.createCesiumRuntime → './CesiumRegionalRuntime', which is the only file importing 'cesium' and 'cesium/Build/Cesium/Widgets/widgets.css', so Cesium JS+CSS load only when 3D is requested; (3) MapLibre's worker is imported with ?worker&url so it is a separate emitted asset; (4) Cesium Workers/Assets/ThirdParty/Widgets are copied to public/cesium by the postinstall script and fetched at runtime via CESIUM_BASE_URL='/cesium/'. There is NO manualChunks or any build/rollupOptions block in vite.config.ts — chunking is whatever Rollup derives from the dynamic imports. Caveats that affect what 'lazy' currently means: main.tsx statically imports 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css' and ten @fontsource CSS files, so MapLibre's CSS is in the entry CSS; InvestigationGraph statically imports AccessPointRelationships → accessPointsApi (Zod), and api/client.ts (entry) imports schemas/priis (Zod), so Zod is in the entry chunk; there is no graph library to defer — both graphs are hand-written SVG. Access-point relationships, the control cross-section, registry features and evidence are lazy at the data level (fetched on demand), not code-split.

special_adjudications.answer: Confirmed. ModuleId is the union command|finance|spatial|anomaly|graph|query; App holds it in useState initialised to 'command' and changes it only through setModule calls from the tab strip, the left rail, the command-bar submit (→ query), Command Center's OPEN QUERY LAYER button and its anomaly cards (→ anomaly). A grep of non-test source for location/history/URLSearchParams/hashchange/popstate finds no code that derives the module from the URL and no hashchange/popstate listener anywhere; the module is not persisted to localStorage either. The only URL consumers are in the Spatial imagery controller: it parses window.location.hash once at mount for map=zoom/lat/lng, eri, op, cmp, fp, base; rewrites the fragment with history.replaceState on moveend and on imagery state changes (skipped while the catalog is loading); and copies window.location.href for 'Copy link'. formatViewHash deletes only its own six keys and preserves any other fragment keys, and the viewHash header states the fragment is free because the app has no router — so a module key in the fragment would survive, but the Spatial controller only runs while the Spatial tab is mounted and its fragment remains in the address bar after leaving the tab. eriApi also reads window.location.origin, and the root ErrorBoundary calls window.location.reload().
